environment.description:
The type of environment must be defined to produce the artifact desired:
 - browser: types are concatenated together as a single JavaScript file
 - node: types are packaged as a Node.js module archive

group.description:
The group of types to be served, supporting the desired API:
 - rest: just REST API wrappers
 - thin: thin client and REST implementations
 - thick: all available implementations

fileName.description:
Optional file name for generated artifact.

This file name is included in the resulting content so it can be saved naturally. More importantly, the
file name affects the artifact content.

For node, If the extension is `.js`, a single JavaScript file is produced with all the classes concatenated.
If the extension is `.tgz`, a Node.js package is produced (a gzipped tar file containing package.json and one
JavaScript file per type).

For browser, the extension must be `.js`, but suffixes to the base name affect how the source is processed.
A `-min` / `_min` suffix causes the code to be minified and a `-es5` / `_es5` suffix causes the code to be
transpiled from ECMAScript 6 to ES5. Multiple suffixes can be used, in any order.  For example
`rest/browser/rest-es5-min.js` will produce a transpiled and minified implementation of the file that can be used
with older browsers.

Note that transpilation will include the necessary polyfills, so sites which already use an ES6 compatibility
layer should probably fetch the native ES6 implementations and apply the compatibility used elsewhere on the page.
Also note that there is no transpilation option for Node.js, so a reasonably current version of node is required.

title:
JavaScript native implementations of the remote APIs are packaged for use within client frameworks, notably the
browser and Node.js.

Note that the API comes in three flavors:
 - rest: simple REST API wrappers
 - thin: lightweight type system proxies
 - thick: full type system instantiated locally

The difference between "thin" and "thick" is in the amount of metadata available in the client.
The thin type system provides lightweight proxy objects which consume and return JavaScript objects without fully
constructing the type system locally. The thick type system has full metadata for each type locally and the types
and objects have all the static and member methods as declared.

This type operates on the builder pattern, with the {@link #produce} function returning the specified client artifact.
It also supports a set of RESTful endpoints that can easily be called from browser `<script>` tags or Node.js
dependencies.
 - `/api/1/remote/rest/node/rest.tgz`: serve the Node.js module for the *rest* API
 - `.../thin/node/thin.tgz`: serve the Node.js module for the *thin* API
 - `.../thick/node/thick.tgz`: serve the Node.js module for the *thick* API
 - `.../rest/browser/rest.js`: serve the browser JavaScript file for the *rest* API
 - `.../thin/browser/thin.js`: serve the browser JavaScript file for the *thin* API
 - `.../thick/browser/thick.js`: serve the browser JavaScrpt file for the *thick* API

See {@link #fileName} for additional options, such as minification and ECMAScript 5 compatibility.
name: RemoteJavaScript
